Keven Murphy &amp; Stefano Maccaglia
1
 " class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_noScript__A7ZNU"/></noscript><div class="thumbnail SlidePreviewThumbnail_thumbnail__tV4CW" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"></div></div></a><div class="" id=":R4329rm:" popover="auto" data-popover-position="bottom-start" style="position-anchor:--popover-R4329rm"></div></div><div class="SlidePreview_root__LBlbv"><a aria-describedby="slide-preview-1" class="slide-preview SlidePreview_preview__YkXou" id="slide-preview-1" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls=":R4529rm:" popovertarget=":R4529rm:" style="anchor-name:--popover-R4529rm" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#2"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp">2<span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp"> / 38</span></span><div class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_root__6KRlr" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"><noscript><img src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-2-2048.jpg" alt="The mass-triage problem in 2018
• The investigation process (Triage), in any IT incident, is the key to solve the case and
to clean all the affected systems.
• But in heterogeneous environments, where Windows, Linux, Mac OS, and Unix
systems are potentially affected by the attacker, the investigation process is slowed
by a number of technical complexities.
 First problem is related to a common platform and procedure to adopt for the triage as many
technologies are capable of covering only a portion of the environment.
 Second problem, what to look for, as the triage is aimed to identify malicious artifacts and usual
technologies are not providing flexibility and agility to shape the triage process.
 Third problem, the capability to search the heterogeneous environment using custom IOCs.
 Fourth problem, the possibility to pinpoint known badness which allows for easier mitigation.
• In our approach, the IOCs play an important role both for the investigation process
and the definition of the best way to approach the triage. We were looking to a
“rule them all” solution aimed to overcome traditional limitations of the most
common commercial solutions.
2
 " class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_noScript__A7ZNU"/></noscript><div class="thumbnail SlidePreviewThumbnail_thumbnail__tV4CW" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"></div></div></a><div class="" id=":R4529rm:" popover="auto" data-popover-position="bottom-start" style="position-anchor:--popover-R4529rm"></div></div><div class="SlidePreview_root__LBlbv"><a aria-describedby="slide-preview-2" class="slide-preview SlidePreview_preview__YkXou" id="slide-preview-2" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls=":R4729rm:" popovertarget=":R4729rm:" style="anchor-name:--popover-R4729rm" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#3"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp">3<span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp"> / 38</span></span><div class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_root__6KRlr" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"><noscript><img src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-3-2048.jpg" alt="Traditional IOCs application
• The traditional IR approach:
• Context, in regard of IOCs, typically does not exists.
• Application of IOCs to the environment is rule-based
• Customization of IOCs are not an option in some commercial products.
• Rule-based detection will miss changes made to the actor’s tools
3
 " class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_noScript__A7ZNU"/></noscript><div class="thumbnail SlidePreviewThumbnail_thumbnail__tV4CW" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"></div></div></a><div class="" id=":R4729rm:" popover="auto" data-popover-position="bottom-start" style="position-anchor:--popover-R4729rm"></div></div><div class="SlidePreview_root__LBlbv"><a aria-describedby="slide-preview-3" class="slide-preview SlidePreview_preview__YkXou" id="slide-preview-3" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls=":R4929rm:" popovertarget=":R4929rm:" style="anchor-name:--popover-R4929rm" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#4"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp">4<span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp"> / 38</span></span><div class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_root__6KRlr" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"><noscript><img src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-4-2048.jpg" alt="Our idea
• The production of code leaves traces in any binary.
• The binary can contain debugging symbols, which give you a lot of information.
• Often the attacker tools include the use of specific libraries or functions.
• A lot of fingerprinting can be done with software, an this is very useful for IR
analyses.
• The combined information of both can help to solve the attribution problem.
• Helps with assessment of risks
• Identifying end goals for known actors
• Aid the creation of IOCs that are “actionable” and not “disposable”
4
 " class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_noScript__A7ZNU"/></noscript><div class="thumbnail SlidePreviewThumbnail_thumbnail__tV4CW" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"></div></div></a><div class="" id=":R4929rm:" popover="auto" data-popover-position="bottom-start" style="position-anchor:--popover-R4929rm"></div></div><div class="SlidePreview_root__LBlbv"><a aria-describedby="slide-preview-4" class="slide-preview SlidePreview_preview__YkXou" id="slide-preview-4" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls=":R4b29rm:" popovertarget=":R4b29rm:" style="anchor-name:--popover-R4b29rm" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#5"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp">5<span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp"> / 38</span></span><div class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_root__6KRlr" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"><noscript><img src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-5-2048.jpg" alt="RIFT (Retrieve Interesting Files Tool)
● Retrieves files/directories based on regex list
● Uses Sleuthkit to retrieve files forensically
● Outputs files files into a directory (machine name)
● Retrieved files are saved remote share/USB
● Recreates the directory structure of where the file was found
● To run:
● Download:
rift --verbose --savedrive [SAVEDRIVE]
https://github.com/chaoticmachinery/frac_rift

 " class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_noScript__A7ZNU"/></noscript><div class="thumbnail SlidePreviewThumbnail_thumbnail__tV4CW" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"></div></div></a><div class="" id=":R4d29rm:" popover="auto" data-popover-position="bottom-start" style="position-anchor:--popover-R4d29rm"></div></div><div class="SlidePreview_root__LBlbv"><a aria-describedby="slide-preview-6" class="slide-preview SlidePreview_preview__YkXou" id="slide-preview-6" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls=":R4f29rm:" popovertarget=":R4f29rm:" style="anchor-name:--popover-R4f29rm" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#7"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp">7<span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp"> / 38</span></span><div class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_root__6KRlr" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"><noscript><img src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-7-2048.jpg" alt="FRAC (Forensic Response ACquisition)
● Uses RIFT to forensically retrieve files/directories across the network
● Recommend using PAExec or SSH/SSHPASS to connect to remote machines
● Requires local admin rights and remote share (SMB/NFS depending on OS)
● Supports single IP, CIDR notation, and IP range like the following examples:
● Can be used to execute any command on remote machines
● To run:
–172.16.10.12
–172.16.10.1/24
–172.16.10.1-172.16.10.230

[SHAREDRV] /delete /yes &amp; net use [SHAREDRV] [SHARE]
/user:[SHAREUSERID] [SHAREPASSWD] &amp;&amp; cd /d [SAVEDRIVE] &amp;&amp; rift.exe --
verbose --savedrive [SAVEDRIVE] &amp;&amp; net use [SHAREDRV] /delete /yes&quot;

[SRCBOX]:[SRCMNT] [SHAREDRV] ; cd [SHAREDRV]/frac_v0.05 &amp;&amp; ./rift --
verbose --savedrive [SAVEDRIVE] ; cd / &amp;&amp; umount [SHAREDRV] &amp;&amp; rmdir

Getfiles.txt
Contains the mactime information for all of the files retrieved as well as the inode
*fls.out
Contains the fls.out (mactime) output from the Sleuthkit FLS command.
All of the directory structure is recreated and files are forensically copied to where
they existed on the drive.

 " class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_noScript__A7ZNU"/></noscript><div class="thumbnail SlidePreviewThumbnail_thumbnail__tV4CW" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"></div></div></a><div class="" id=":R4h29rm:" popover="auto" data-popover-position="bottom-start" style="position-anchor:--popover-R4h29rm"></div></div><div class="SlidePreview_root__LBlbv"><a aria-describedby="slide-preview-8" class="slide-preview SlidePreview_preview__YkXou" id="slide-preview-8" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls=":R4j29rm:" popovertarget=":R4j29rm:" style="anchor-name:--popover-R4j29rm" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#9"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp">9<span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp"> / 38</span></span><div class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_root__6KRlr" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"><noscript><img src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-9-2048.jpg" alt="Actionable IOCs (AIOCs)
• The concept of “actionable” IOCs has been derived and refined from a collective set of
Incident Response investigations, and could become a valid support of our investigative
process if organized in a scientifically sound approach.
• Utilizes procedures, analysis, and evidence for a methodical approach
• Based on positive matches can help identify the attacker
• It allow the creation of a structured knowledge base of attackers
• The knowledge base allows the creation of attacker profiles

 " class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_noScript__A7ZNU"/></noscript><div class="thumbnail SlidePreviewThumbnail_thumbnail__tV4CW" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"></div></div></a><div class="" id=":R4l29rm:" popover="auto" data-popover-position="bottom-start" style="position-anchor:--popover-R4l29rm"></div></div><div class="SlidePreview_root__LBlbv"><a aria-describedby="slide-preview-10" class="slide-preview SlidePreview_preview__YkXou" id="slide-preview-10" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls=":R4n29rm:" popovertarget=":R4n29rm:" style="anchor-name:--popover-R4n29rm" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#11"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp">11<span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp"> / 38</span></span><div class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_root__6KRlr" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"><noscript><img src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-11-2048.jpg" alt="Example: PoisonIvy
• PoisonIvy, a Remote Access Tool/Trojan (RAT) often used in targeted attacks, had been
widely seen until around 2013.
• Since then, the number of cases using PoisonIvy decreased, and there was no special
variant with expanded features seen in the wild.
• However, recently, we identified PoisonIvy with expanded features in its communication
function capable to bypass HTTP/HTTPS proxy in APT and cybercriminal attacks thanks to
modifications in the malware code.
Latest PoisonIvy variants are different

It is a backdoor.
• The malware can be split into two components:
 the main module,
 communication module.
• The main module is responsible for providing the framework to execute the various
components within the malware.
• The communication module is responsible for the sending of information to the server,
receiving new commands from it and downloading of new executable.
• If a new executable is downloaded successfully, it will notifying the main
module to execute it.
• The malware is capable of:
• Listing and controlling processes
• Creating and deleting files
• Creating a remote shell
• Downloading and executing files
• Bisonal is an APT tool.

o Type of malware: Modular Trojan (single stage), mainly used for data stealing
o Capabilities: beaconing, listing and controlling processes, creating and deleting files, creating
remote shells, downloading and executing files
o Dissemination strategy: via Dropper or email attachment
o Architecture: Client / Server using public C2s
o Type of communication: HTTP protocol (in general it uses TCP/80 and TCP/443, but port can be
customized)
o Related Adversary: HeartBeat APT Group (Chinese)
o Earlier Adversary detection: November 2009 (South Korea - TrendMicro)
o Area of operation: actually limited to Asia (including Russia)
o Recorded targets: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, NEC Corp, Nippon Steel Corp, IHI Corp, several
Ministries in Japan and South Korea.
o Type of AIOCs developed: Yara rules for files, Yara rules for PCAPs, ClamAV rules, Snort Rule,
Registry and logs.

Clam AV: Intro
• ClamAV is an open source and free anti-virus program.
• ClamAV runs on Windows (ClamWin), Linux, BSD, Solaris, and Mac OS X, and its
mainly designed to scan email attachment, but it can be used as a regular anti-
virus.
• ClamAV includes:
• Features
• Can search archives
• Can search multiple file types
• Multithreaded
 Clamscan
 Clamdscan/Clamd
 Freshclam
Command line virus scanner
Client/Server virus scanner
tool to update the virus definition database

YARA Rules, AIOCs and ClamAV
• Yara is the swiss army knife for any low-cost triage and can be applied to many
endpoint forensic platforms.
• Values that work across multiple platforms
• Text strings
• Hex values that are in multiple versions of the binary
• ClamAV provides combination of both worlds.
• By empowering ClamAV with Yara rules, we are able to run massive triage on almost all type
of system using AIOCs we have developed.

sigFile.mdb
• To create a unique signature for an executable file we use the --md5 option of
sigtool, and then save the output into a file with a “.hdb” extension.
• To create a signature that will match a particular PE section (typically the sections are
labelled .text, .rdata, .data, .idata, etc.), use the “--mdb” option of sigtool and then save
the output into a “.mdb” file. The easiest way to generate MD5 based section signatures is
to extract target PE sections into separate files.

0,2 and 3) OR (only strings 4 and 5) OR (both strings 6,7
and 8).

• The adoption of this methodology can positively impact investigation and triage, but also

• The formalization process behind it can facilitate the exchange of information and

 " class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_noScript__A7ZNU"/></noscript><div class="thumbnail SlidePreviewThumbnail_thumbnail__tV4CW" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"></div></div></a><div class="" id=":R6b29rm:" popover="auto" data-popover-position="bottom-start" style="position-anchor:--popover-R6b29rm"></div></div><div class="SlidePreview_root__LBlbv"><a aria-describedby="slide-preview-37" class="slide-preview SlidePreview_preview__YkXou" id="slide-preview-37" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls=":R6d29rm:" popovertarget=":R6d29rm:" style="anchor-name:--popover-R6d29rm" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#38"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp">38<span class="text Text_root__RtCPC text-secondary weight-regular Text_xsmall__X6YLp"> / 38</span></span><div class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_root__6KRlr" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"><noscript><img src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-38-2048.jpg" alt="Thanks!
 " class="SlidePreviewThumbnail_noScript__A7ZNU"/></noscript><div class="thumbnail SlidePreviewThumbnail_thumbnail__tV4CW" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540"></div></div></a><div class="" id=":R6d29rm:" popover="auto" data-popover-position="bottom-start" style="position-anchor:--popover-R6d29rm"></div></div></div></div><div class="player vertical-player VerticalPlayer_root__K8_YS" data-cy="vertical-player" data-slideshow-id="97098401"><div id="slide1" class="VerticalSlide_root__jU_9r slide-item" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540" data-cy="slide-container"><div class="VerticalSlideImage_root__64KSA"><img id="slide-image-0" alt="Practical Incident Response in
Heterogeneous Environment
Keven Murphy &amp; Stefano Maccaglia
1
 " data-testid="vertical-slide-image" fetchpriority="high" loading="eager" decoding="async" data-nimg="fill" style="position:absolute;height:100%;width:100%;left:0;top:0;right:0;bottom:0;color:transparent" src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-1-2048.jpg"/></div><div></div></div><div id="slide2" class="VerticalSlide_root__jU_9r slide-item" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540" data-cy="slide-container"><div class="VerticalSlideImage_root__64KSA"><img id="slide-image-1" alt="The mass-triage problem in 2018
• The investigation process (Triage), in any IT incident, is the key to solve the case and
to clean all the affected systems.
• But in heterogeneous environments, where Windows, Linux, Mac OS, and Unix
systems are potentially affected by the attacker, the investigation process is slowed
by a number of technical complexities.
 First problem is related to a common platform and procedure to adopt for the triage as many
technologies are capable of covering only a portion of the environment.
 Second problem, what to look for, as the triage is aimed to identify malicious artifacts and usual
technologies are not providing flexibility and agility to shape the triage process.
 Third problem, the capability to search the heterogeneous environment using custom IOCs.
 Fourth problem, the possibility to pinpoint known badness which allows for easier mitigation.
• In our approach, the IOCs play an important role both for the investigation process
and the definition of the best way to approach the triage. We were looking to a
“rule them all” solution aimed to overcome traditional limitations of the most
common commercial solutions.
2
 " data-testid="vertical-slide-image" fetchpriority="high" loading="eager" decoding="async" data-nimg="fill" style="position:absolute;height:100%;width:100%;left:0;top:0;right:0;bottom:0;color:transparent" src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-2-2048.jpg"/></div><div></div></div><div id="slide3" class="VerticalSlide_root__jU_9r slide-item" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540" data-cy="slide-container"><div class="VerticalSlideImage_root__64KSA"><img id="slide-image-2" alt="Traditional IOCs application
• The traditional IR approach:
• Context, in regard of IOCs, typically does not exists.
• Application of IOCs to the environment is rule-based
• Customization of IOCs are not an option in some commercial products.
• Rule-based detection will miss changes made to the actor’s tools
3
 " data-testid="vertical-slide-image" loading="lazy" decoding="async" data-nimg="fill" style="position:absolute;height:100%;width:100%;left:0;top:0;right:0;bottom:0;color:transparent" src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-3-2048.jpg"/></div><div></div></div><div id="slide4" class="VerticalSlide_root__jU_9r slide-item" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540" data-cy="slide-container"><div class="VerticalSlideImage_root__64KSA"><img id="slide-image-3" alt="Our idea
• The production of code leaves traces in any binary.
• The binary can contain debugging symbols, which give you a lot of information.
• Often the attacker tools include the use of specific libraries or functions.
• A lot of fingerprinting can be done with software, an this is very useful for IR
analyses.
• The combined information of both can help to solve the attribution problem.
• Helps with assessment of risks
• Identifying end goals for known actors
• Aid the creation of IOCs that are “actionable” and not “disposable”

 " data-testid="vertical-slide-image" loading="lazy" decoding="async" data-nimg="fill" style="position:absolute;height:100%;width:100%;left:0;top:0;right:0;bottom:0;color:transparent" src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-4-2048.jpg"/></div><div></div></div><div id="slide5" class="VerticalSlide_root__jU_9r slide-item" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540" data-cy="slide-container"><div class="VerticalSlideImage_root__64KSA"><img id="slide-image-4" alt="RIFT (Retrieve Interesting Files Tool)
● Retrieves files/directories based on regex list
● Uses Sleuthkit to retrieve files forensically
● Outputs files files into a directory (machine name)
● Retrieved files are saved remote share/USB
● Recreates the directory structure of where the file was found
● To run:
● Download:
rift --verbose --savedrive [SAVEDRIVE]
https://github.com/chaoticmachinery/frac_rift

Getfiles.txt
Contains the mactime information for all of the files retrieved as well as the inode
*fls.out
Contains the fls.out (mactime) output from the Sleuthkit FLS command.
All of the directory structure is recreated and files are forensically copied to where

 " data-testid="vertical-slide-image" loading="lazy" decoding="async" data-nimg="fill" style="position:absolute;height:100%;width:100%;left:0;top:0;right:0;bottom:0;color:transparent" src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-8-2048.jpg"/></div><div></div></div><div id="slide9" class="VerticalSlide_root__jU_9r slide-item" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540" data-cy="slide-container"><div class="VerticalSlideImage_root__64KSA"><img id="slide-image-8" alt="Actionable IOCs (AIOCs)
• The concept of “actionable” IOCs has been derived and refined from a collective set of
Incident Response investigations, and could become a valid support of our investigative
process if organized in a scientifically sound approach.
• Utilizes procedures, analysis, and evidence for a methodical approach
• Based on positive matches can help identify the attacker
• It allow the creation of a structured knowledge base of attackers
• The knowledge base allows the creation of attacker profiles

 " data-testid="vertical-slide-image" loading="lazy" decoding="async" data-nimg="fill" style="position:absolute;height:100%;width:100%;left:0;top:0;right:0;bottom:0;color:transparent" src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-10-2048.jpg"/></div><div></div></div><div id="slide11" class="VerticalSlide_root__jU_9r slide-item" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540" data-cy="slide-container"><div class="VerticalSlideImage_root__64KSA"><img id="slide-image-10" alt="Example: PoisonIvy
• PoisonIvy, a Remote Access Tool/Trojan (RAT) often used in targeted attacks, had been
widely seen until around 2013.
• Since then, the number of cases using PoisonIvy decreased, and there was no special
variant with expanded features seen in the wild.
• However, recently, we identified PoisonIvy with expanded features in its communication
function capable to bypass HTTP/HTTPS proxy in APT and cybercriminal attacks thanks to
modifications in the malware code.
Latest PoisonIvy variants are different

• The malware can be split into two components:
 the main module,
 communication module.
• The main module is responsible for providing the framework to execute the various
components within the malware.
• The communication module is responsible for the sending of information to the server,
receiving new commands from it and downloading of new executable.
• If a new executable is downloaded successfully, it will notifying the main
module to execute it.
• The malware is capable of:
• Listing and controlling processes
• Creating and deleting files
• Creating a remote shell
• Downloading and executing files
• Bisonal is an APT tool.

Clam AV: Intro
• ClamAV is an open source and free anti-virus program.
• ClamAV runs on Windows (ClamWin), Linux, BSD, Solaris, and Mac OS X, and its
mainly designed to scan email attachment, but it can be used as a regular anti-
virus.
• ClamAV includes:
• Features
• Can search archives
• Can search multiple file types
• Multithreaded
 Clamscan
 Clamdscan/Clamd
 Freshclam
Command line virus scanner
Client/Server virus scanner
tool to update the virus definition database
 " data-testid="vertical-slide-image" loading="lazy" decoding="async" data-nimg="fill" style="position:absolute;height:100%;width:100%;left:0;top:0;right:0;bottom:0;color:transparent" src="https://image.slidesharecdn.com/bsidesfinal-180515003159/75/BSides-IR-in-Heterogeneous-Environment-22-2048.jpg"/></div><div></div></div><div id="slide23" class="VerticalSlide_root__jU_9r slide-item" style="aspect-ratio:960 / 540" data-cy="slide-container"><div class="VerticalSlideImage_root__64KSA"><img id="slide-image-22" alt="23
YARA Rules, AIOCs and ClamAV
• Yara is the swiss army knife for any low-cost triage and can be applied to many
endpoint forensic platforms.
• Values that work across multiple platforms
• Text strings
• Hex values that are in multiple versions of the binary
• ClamAV provides combination of both worlds.
• By empowering ClamAV with Yara rules, we are able to run massive triage on almost all type
of system using AIOCs we have developed.

sigFile.mdb
• To create a unique signature for an executable file we use the --md5 option of
sigtool, and then save the output into a file with a “.hdb” extension.
• To create a signature that will match a particular PE section (typically the sections are
labelled .text, .rdata, .data, .idata, etc.), use the “--mdb” option of sigtool and then save
the output into a “.mdb” file. The easiest way to generate MD5 based section signatures is
to extract target PE sections into separate files.

• The last method is to use Body-based signatures in an hexadecimal format.
It relies on extracted strings from the body of the file.

MalwareName:TargetType:Offset:HexSignature and redirect the
output to a file “.ndb”.

PoisonIVY2011UPX:0:*:76727937666f2f55524c446f776e657a7b*365c5c7525752e3139332e2564
The second part contains instead
“CONNECT %s:%i HTTP//1.0”
The first Rule contains two non-successive strings divided by the symbol “*”. The first
string translated from hexadecimal contains the word
“%supdate%4d%02d%02d%02d%02d%02d.tmp”.
This rule takes a Poison Ivy sample dated 2011 and we use 3 different
strings. The first is “/c del %s &gt; nul”
The second strings is
“GET %s HTTP/1.1”
The last matches to
“uuddosbea”
The third rule is the same sample
mentioned above, but without the
package UPX. The first of two strings
is “vry7fo/URLDownez{”
The second strings is
“6u%u.193.%d”

BISONAL;Target:1;(0&amp;1&amp;2)|(0&amp;2&amp;3)|(4&amp;5)|(6&amp;7&amp;8)
This is a ClamAV “Body-based”, slightly different, from
the previous one. It has to be put inside a “.LDB” file
and it is possible to use logic operators inside the rule.
Logical operators in action within the BISONAL signature.
Numbers are placeholders for the hex strings.
Match IF found: (both strings 0,1 and 2) OR (both strings
0,2 and 3) OR (only strings 4 and 5) OR (both strings 6,7
and 8).

class="sr-only"></span></span></span></button></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div></div><div><div class="transcript Transcript_root__Vrf6Q"><div class="Transcript_wrapper__gIgMH"><h2 class="heading Heading_root__KdmZo weight-medium Heading_xxsmall__oA9Tv">BSides IR in Heterogeneous Environment</h2><ul class="Transcript_list__faItj" style="--bullet-size:2ch"><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">1. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#1">Practical Incident Response</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">in
Heterogeneous Environment
Keven Murphy &amp; Stefano Maccaglia
1
 </span></div></li><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">2. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#2">The mass-triage problem</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">in 2018
• The investigation process (Triage), in any IT incident, is the key to solve the case and
to clean all the affected systems.
• But in heterogeneous environments, where Windows, Linux, Mac OS, and Unix
systems are potentially affected by the attacker, the investigation process is slowed
by a number of technical complexities.
 First problem is related to a common platform and procedure to adopt for the triage as many
technologies are capable of covering only a portion of the environment.
 Second problem, what to look for, as the triage is aimed to identify malicious artifacts and usual
technologies are not providing flexibility and agility to shape the triage process.
 Third problem, the capability to search the heterogeneous environment using custom IOCs.
 Fourth problem, the possibility to pinpoint known badness which allows for easier mitigation.
• In our approach, the IOCs play an important role both for the investigation process
and the definition of the best way to approach the triage. We were looking to a
“rule them all” solution aimed to overcome traditional limitations of the most
common commercial solutions.
2
 </span></div></li><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">3. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#3">Traditional IOCs application
•</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">The traditional IR approach:
• Context, in regard of IOCs, typically does not exists.
• Application of IOCs to the environment is rule-based
• Customization of IOCs are not an option in some commercial products.
• Rule-based detection will miss changes made to the actor’s tools
3
 </span></div></li><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">4. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#4">Our idea
• The</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">production of code leaves traces in any binary.
• The binary can contain debugging symbols, which give you a lot of information.
• Often the attacker tools include the use of specific libraries or functions.
• A lot of fingerprinting can be done with software, an this is very useful for IR
analyses.
• The combined information of both can help to solve the attribution problem.
• Helps with assessment of risks
• Identifying end goals for known actors
• Aid the creation of IOCs that are “actionable” and not “disposable”
4
 </span></div></li><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">5. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#5">RIFT (Retrieve Interesting</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">Files Tool)

● Outputs files files into a directory (machine name)
● Retrieved files are saved remote share/USB
● Recreates the directory structure of where the file was found
● To run:

 </span></div></li><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">9. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#9">Actionable IOCs (AIOCs)
•</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">The concept of “actionable” IOCs has been derived and refined from a collective set of
Incident Response investigations, and could become a valid support of our investigative
process if organized in a scientifically sound approach.
• Utilizes procedures, analysis, and evidence for a methodical approach
• Based on positive matches can help identify the attacker
• It allow the creation of a structured knowledge base of attackers
• The knowledge base allows the creation of attacker profiles

 </span></div></li><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">11. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#11">Example: PoisonIvy
• PoisonIvy,</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">a Remote Access Tool/Trojan (RAT) often used in targeted attacks, had been
widely seen until around 2013.
• Since then, the number of cases using PoisonIvy decreased, and there was no special
variant with expanded features seen in the wild.
• However, recently, we identified PoisonIvy with expanded features in its communication
function capable to bypass HTTP/HTTPS proxy in APT and cybercriminal attacks thanks to
modifications in the malware code.
Latest PoisonIvy variants are different

 </span></div></li><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">15. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#15">• Bisonal is</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">another example. It is a backdoor.
• The malware can be split into two components:
 the main module,
 communication module.
• The main module is responsible for providing the framework to execute the various
components within the malware.
• The communication module is responsible for the sending of information to the server,
receiving new commands from it and downloading of new executable.
• If a new executable is downloaded successfully, it will notifying the main
module to execute it.
• The malware is capable of:
• Listing and controlling processes
• Creating and deleting files
• Creating a remote shell
• Downloading and executing files
• Bisonal is an APT tool.
Trojan.Bisonal

o Type of malware: Modular Trojan (single stage), mainly used for data stealing
o Capabilities: beaconing, listing and controlling processes, creating and deleting files, creating
remote shells, downloading and executing files
o Dissemination strategy: via Dropper or email attachment
o Architecture: Client / Server using public C2s
o Type of communication: HTTP protocol (in general it uses TCP/80 and TCP/443, but port can be
customized)
o Related Adversary: HeartBeat APT Group (Chinese)
o Earlier Adversary detection: November 2009 (South Korea - TrendMicro)
o Area of operation: actually limited to Asia (including Russia)
o Recorded targets: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, NEC Corp, Nippon Steel Corp, IHI Corp, several
Ministries in Japan and South Korea.
o Type of AIOCs developed: Yara rules for files, Yara rules for PCAPs, ClamAV rules, Snort Rule,
Registry and logs.

Clam AV: Intro
•</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">ClamAV is an open source and free anti-virus program.
• ClamAV runs on Windows (ClamWin), Linux, BSD, Solaris, and Mac OS X, and its
mainly designed to scan email attachment, but it can be used as a regular anti-
virus.
• ClamAV includes:
• Features
• Can search archives
• Can search multiple file types
• Multithreaded
 Clamscan
 Clamdscan/Clamd
 Freshclam
Command line virus scanner
Client/Server virus scanner
tool to update the virus definition database
 </span></div></li><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">23. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#23">23
YARA Rules, AIOCs</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">and ClamAV
• Yara is the swiss army knife for any low-cost triage and can be applied to many
endpoint forensic platforms.
• Values that work across multiple platforms
• Text strings
• Hex values that are in multiple versions of the binary
• ClamAV provides combination of both worlds.
• By empowering ClamAV with Yara rules, we are able to run massive triage on almost all type
of system using AIOCs we have developed.
 </span></div></li><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">24. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#24">Using ClamAV to</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">Scan for Badness

 </span></div></li><li class="TranscriptItem_root__SYFxL"><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_medium__TH6gG">28. </span><div><a class="link Link_root__vn3ab Link_primary__Iq4CI weight-regular Link_large__8fEbX" href="https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/bsides-ir-in-heterogeneous-environment/97098401#28">C:Documents and SettingsuserDesktop&gt;</a><span class="text Text_root__RtCPC weight-regular Text_small__HLf8O">sigtool --md5 malware.exe &gt;&gt; sigFile.hdb
C:Documents and SettingsuserDesktop&gt;type sigFile.hdb
B4619d8058362b38d20480c14d30c209:40500:malware.exe
C:Documents and SettingsuserDesktop&gt; sigtool --mdb malware.exe.text.dat &gt;&gt;
sigFile.mdb
• To create a unique signature for an executable file we use the --md5 option of
sigtool, and then save the output into a file with a “.hdb” extension.
• To create a signature that will match a particular PE section (typically the sections are
labelled .text, .rdata, .data, .idata, etc.), use the “--mdb” option of sigtool and then save
the output into a “.mdb” file. The easiest way to generate MD5 based section signatures is
to extract target PE sections into separate files.

• The last method is to use Body-based signatures in an hexadecimal format.
It relies on extracted strings from the body of the file.
• In the next example we create an hex dump of the string “I am malware”.
• Next we save the signature that has the format called “Extended Signature”:
MalwareName:TargetType:Offset:HexSignature and redirect the
output to a file “.ndb”.

Logical operators in action within the BISONAL signature.

0,2 and 3) OR (only strings 4 and 5) OR (both strings 6,7
and 8).

attribution and the triage, of incidents generated by malicious actors.
• The adoption of this methodology can positively impact investigation and triage, but also
improves knowledge of the tools and strategies adopted by the adversaries.
• The formalization process behind it can facilitate the exchange of information and
indicators without the risk of unintentional leakage of sensitive information and, in short,
strengthen the proactive and reactive capabilities of any structure.

to adopt for the triage as many\ntechnologies are capable of covering only a portion of the environment.\n Second problem, what to look for, as the triage is aimed to identify malicious artifacts and usual\ntechnologies are not providing flexibility and agility to shape the triage process.\n Third problem, the capability to search the heterogeneous environment using custom IOCs.\n Fourth problem, the possibility to pinpoint known badness which allows for easier mitigation.\n• In our approach, the IOCs play an important role both for the investigation process\nand the definition of the best way to approach the triage. We were looking to a\n“rule them all” solution aimed to overcome traditional limitations of the most\ncommon commercial solutions.\n2\n ","Traditional IOCs application\n• The traditional IR approach:\n• Context, in regard of IOCs, typically does not exists.\n• Application of IOCs to the environment is rule-based\n• Customization of IOCs are not an option in some commercial products.\n• Rule-based detection will miss changes made to the actor’s tools\n3\n ","Our idea\n• The production of code leaves traces in any binary.\n• The binary can contain debugging symbols, which give you a lot of information.\n• Often the attacker tools include the use of specific libraries or functions.\n• A lot of fingerprinting can be done with software, an this is very useful for IR\nanalyses.\n• The combined information of both can help to solve the attribution problem.\n• Helps with assessment of risks\n• Identifying end goals for known actors\n• Aid the creation of IOCs that are “actionable” and not “disposable”\n4\n ","RIFT (Retrieve Interesting Files Tool)\n● Retrieves files/directories based on regex list\n● Uses Sleuthkit to retrieve files forensically\n● Outputs files
